messages:
Maya: Heads-up — I'm prototyping a Console flow for A/B experiments that focuses on safety/quotas first. Want quick feedback on UX and API shape.
Alex: love that. what do you mean by safety/quotas first?
Maya: two things: 1) enforce per-variant request caps so a runaway variant can't burn Dedicated capacity and 2) require telemetry keys + min-sample thresholds before ramping to >10% traffic.
Ben: +1. we need automatic fallback to baseline if latency or error rate regresses >X. Otherwise ops will hate us.
Sasha: is the idea to push most policy enforcement into the control plane (console/API) or keep minimal UI checks and let the router enforce at runtime?
Maya: prefer control plane validation + router enforcement. Console should block obviously invalid configs and surface guard recommendations. Router still needs runtime guards (rate limiter, quota token checks, variant isolation).
Ryan: do we have an API shape drafted? I worry about back-compat if we add guard fields later.
Maya: sketch below — it's intentionally explicit about guards:
```json
{
  "experiment_id": "exp_checkout_prompt_v2",
  "variants": [
    {"id":"baseline","weight":70},
    {"id":"v2","weight":30,"max_qps":50}
  ],
  "rollout": {
    "phases": [
      {"percent":5, "duration_minutes":60},
      {"percent":30, "duration_minutes":180}
    ],
    "min_effective_samples": 1000,
    "metrics_watchlist": ["latency_p95","error_rate"]
  },
  "guards": {
    "quota_check": "enforced",
    "fallback_variant": "baseline",
    "auto_pause_on_regression": true
  },
  "telemetry_keys": ["route_id","customer_tier"]
}
```
Alex: nice. a few thoughts: rename `min_effective_samples` to `min_n_effective`? also phase durations should support cron-like windows for region-specific ramping.
Ben: also need an explicit `capacity_reservation` hint so Dedicated can lock GPUs for high-weight variants. UI should warn if requested capacity > available.
Sasha: on the console side, the wizard should: 1) show a preflight checker that simulates traffic split and highlights quota hot-spots; 2) disable >X% ramp if no telemetry attached; 3) require a rollback target.
Maya: agree. preflight could run a lightweight simulation using historical traffic. Might surface expected token cost delta.
Ryan: telemetry_keys are tricky — many customers don't have route-level keys. We should allow a temporary opt-out but surface extra guard rigor (lower ramp ceiling) if keys missing.
Ben: for runtime guards, suggest we implement a circuit-breaker per-variant: track a short-window error rate and if it crosses threshold, reduce weight by a configured step and pause rollout.
Sasha: UI microcopy idea: "Canary recommendations: start small, attach telemetry to get faster ramps, reserve capacity if using Dedicated." Keep it prescriptive.
Maya: what about quotas? Should console set per-variant QPS caps automatically based on model throughput?
Alex: we can suggest caps based on model profile in catalog (tokens/sec) and customer Dedicated pool size. But make it editable.
Maya: also ask whether we should persist experiment as immutable revisioned object (so rollbacks are applying previous revision) or mutable.
Ryan: go immutable — easier audit and replay. But console can expose a "reopen" action that creates a new revision from an old one.
Ben: telemetry: define required fields we collect at rollout time (latency, tokens, errors, route_id). We should add `traffic_bucket` so we can compute variance quickly.
Maya: good call. add to schema: `telemetry_required: ["latency_p95","error_rate","tokens_consumed","route_id","traffic_bucket"]`.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: staging -> canary guard tests at 2026-11-12T15:00Z :white_check_mark:
Sasha: small nit: how do we handle multi-variant (>2) experiments in the wizard? UX gets messy when you need to set individual caps/guards for 6 variants.
Maya: plan: default to global rollout policy for N>3 and provide an "advanced" tab for per-variant overrides. Also provide a reorderable list for priority fallback.
Alex: telemetry-based early stop: add an `early_stop_rule` with expression language, e.g., `error_rate[v2] - error_rate[baseline] > 0.02 for 3m`. We can reuse our existing alert DSL.
Ben: question on data retention and evals: should Console automatically run a small AB analysis job after each phase? Even a simple t-test and a practical significance check would be helpful.
Maya: yes — call it "phase evaluation". Console should run it and surface whether metric deltas passed thresholds. If not, auto-pause.
Sasha: one more: for Dedicated customers, include a "billing impact" estimate on the wizard — tokens * price per token delta. Ops and PMs love that.
Maya: thanks. I'll iterate on the API shape and wire a preflight simulation endpoint: `POST /internal/experiments/simulate` that returns hotspots and expected QPS per route.
Alex: assign me for the router guard API and I'll prototype enforcement hooks.
Ben: I'll mock the evaluation job and an example report payload.
Sasha: I'll draft the wizard screens and error states. low-fidelity first.
Maya: perfect. I'll update the spec and post a follow-up thread with the new JSON and preflight example. :thumbsup:
Ryan: great work, team.
Maya: (cc @deploy-bot) triggering a staging run once Alex's guard PR is up.
deploy-bot: CI: experiments/guard-api #342 passed. staging deploy queued.
Ben: :eyes:
Alex: landed a small proto in the router branch, will open PR tomorrow.
Maya: thanks everyone — closing this sync.
